app.title: Beam Calculator
app.subtitle: Finite element analysis of single and continuous beams
app.mobileViewOnly: On narrow screens (< 768 px) results can only be viewed. Please use a larger window for editing.
app.footer: Linear static analysis, first-order theory. All calculations run locally in your browser. Express checks do not replace a code check.

beam.name: Project name
beam.segmentsHint: The beam can be divided into segments with different cross-sections or materials.
beam.author: Engineer

section.label: Cross-section
section.periPermNote: Checked with permissible values (perm M, perm Q, perm R) under service loads 1.0·G + 1.0·Q; I from the chords, E = 11,000 N/mm².
section.periDesignNote: Checked with the design resistances N_Rd, V_z,Rd, M_y,Rd of the net sections A 4-4, A 5-5 and B 2-2 and the interaction n–v, v–m, n–v–m (ULS). No stability check.
section.periGirderNote: Checked with the MULTIFLEX design values (V_Rd, M_Rd, support force F_R,d per support case) for the ULS combinations; edge distance of the end supports. I from the chords, E = 11,000 N/mm².
section.periEc3Note: Checked per EN 1993-1-1 6.2.10 (N–V–M interaction, Wagenknecht) on the net section with bolt holes, γ_M1 = 1.1 (ULS). No stability check.
section.periAtNode: Supports under a lattice node (MULTIFLEX case 1 / 3)
section.periAtNodeHint: Unchecked: supports between the nodes (case 2 / 4, on the safe side: F_R,d = 19.5 / 30 kN, M_m,Rd = 6 kNm).
section.periLatticeNote: Member model as the PERI RSTAB model (continuous chords, pin-ended diagonals, gap nodes, standard between elastic couplers). Checks after PERI: ULS – cross-sections of chords (n, v, m) and diagonals (n, v, m_N), without buckling and welds; standard – flexural buckling (curve b, L_cr); couplers – slipping (15 / 25 kN : 1.1); ULS Flex – permissible loads of the PERI configurations. ULA HD: EN 1999-1-1 with heat affected zone.
section.flexElements: ULS Flex elements (end element 50 + intermediate elements + end element 50)
section.latticeRestraint: Lateral restraint of the top chord every
section.latticeEccentric: Nodes with gap g as in the PERI RSTAB model (eccentric)
section.latticeEccentricHint: Checked (default): diagonals with a gap of 65 / 79 mm at the chord as in the PERI drawings and RSTAB models – internal forces agree with RSTAB. Unchecked: centric nodes (reproduces the PERI table values).
section.couplerHint: As in the PERI RSTAB model: standard between the couplers as a member, each coupler an elastic support of the chord (default 9100 / 10 kN/m).

material.label: Material
material.expressNote: express check, not a code check
material.periLocked: PERI component: material as specified by the manufacturer, cannot be changed (checks use the PERI values).

support.title: Supports
support.springHint: Spring stiffness per direction; 0 = no spring. Spring force = k · displacement.
support.legend: Fixed: u, w, θ restrained · Pinned: u, w · Roller: w · Sliding sleeve: u, θ (w free) · Spring: springs k_u, k_w, k_θ

hinge.title: Hinges
hinge.hint: Hinge: common displacements u, w, separate rotations θ₁ ≠ θ₂, M = 0.

load.signs: Signs: x to the right, z (deflection) positive downwards. Force angle α measured clockwise from +x (90° = vertically down). Distributed load q > 0 acts downwards, axial load p > 0 in +x. Moment M > 0 clockwise. If q₁ = q₂, editing q₁ changes both values.

lc.title: Load cases
lc.inUse: Load case is used by loads
lc.selfWeightHint: The self weight is assigned automatically to the first load case of category G.

combo.title: Combinations
combo.hint: Default: ULS 1.5·G + 1.5·Q (formwork/falsework, γ_F = 1.5 as in the PERI design information) and 1.0·G + 1.5·Q (favourable G), SLS 1.0·G + 1.0·Q. The strength check uses the ULS, the deflection check the SLS combinations.

settings.selfWeightHint: q_sw = ρ · A · g (g = 9.81 m/s²), per segment
settings.patternLoadingHint: For load cases of category Q all combinations of loaded spans are investigated (envelope).
settings.limitsHint: Limits for the deflection check with the SLS combinations: L = span length, L_c = cantilever length. Typical: L/250 and L_c/125.
settings.upliftCheckHint: Pinned and roller supports take compression only: if the beam lifts off (R_z > 0 in any combination), the support fails.

results.cursorHint: Move the mouse over the schematic or diagrams to read all values at position x.
results.none: No results – please check the input.
results.signs: Sign convention (DIN): N > 0 tension; V > 0 acts in +z on the positive cut face; M > 0 causes tension at the bottom. Deflection w > 0 downwards.

schematic.label: Structural system
schematic.standardHint: Lattice girder: click the circles below the bottom chord to place or remove standards with couplers (ULA / ULS) or supports at standards and connectors (ULS Flex).

kpi.reactionSigns: Support reactions in the global axes of the drawing (z downwards): R_x > 0 to the right (→), R_z > 0 downwards (↓), M_R > 0 clockwise (↻). A support pushing the beam up has R_z < 0.
kpi.expressNote: Express check, not a code check (no stability checks).
kpi.basisULS: Basis: envelope of the ULS combinations
kpi.basisSLS: Basis: envelope of the SLS combinations
kpi.periBasisSLS: Basis: service loads (characteristic combinations, SLS), perm F = R_d/1.5
kpi.periEdge: Edge distance of the end support
kpi.basisChar: Basis: characteristic combination of all load cases (no SLS combination)

lattice.head: ledger heads UH Plus at the rosette
lattice.restraints: Ticks above the top chord: lateral restraints
lattice.mechanism: The member model is a mechanism (check the supports).

mode.periChord: cross-section after PERI: n, v, m
mode.periDiag: cross-section after PERI: n, v, m_N
mode.standard: flexural buckling of the standard, curve b

lattice.flexMissing: no PERI configuration for these elements – no check possible, please choose a configuration of the table.

err.positive: The value must be greater than 0.
err.nonNegative: The value must not be negative.
err.range: The value must be between {min} and {max}.
err.order: x₂ must be greater than x₁.
err.segmentEnd: The last segment must end at x = {x}.
err.noSegments: At least one segment is required.
err.unknownSection: Profile not found in the section table.
err.wallTooThick: Plate/wall thickness too large for the dimensions.

warn.hingeAtEnd: A hinge at the beam end has no effect and is ignored.
warn.duplicateHinge: Several hinges at the same position – only one is used.
warn.hingeAtClamp: Hinge at a fixed support (or sliding sleeve/rotational spring): the rotation is not restrained, the support acts as a pinned support.
warn.duplicateSupport: Several supports at the same position.
warn.duplicateRestraint: DOF already restrained by another support – the reaction is assigned to the first support.
warn.illConditioned: Stiffness matrix is ill-conditioned (κ ≈ {cond}). Please check the results.
warn.noGCase: No load case of category G – the self weight is not applied.
warn.latticeMixed: Lattice girder: the beam must consist of one lattice girder only – no member model check.
warn.latticeLength: Lattice girder: the length is not a catalogue length ({lengths} m); the nodes are arranged from the girder end.
warn.flexLength: ULS Flex: the elements give the system length {L} m, not the beam length.

mech.noX: No restraint in x direction: at least one pinned support, fixed support or sliding sleeve is required.
mech.rotation: Kinematically unstable: the beam can rotate about the support at x = {x}. Add another support or a fixed support.
mech.twoHinges: Mechanism: two consecutive hinges (x = {x1} and x = {x2}) without a support in between.
mech.part: Mechanism: the region between x = {x1} and x = {x2} is kinematically unstable (too many hinges or too few supports).
mech.numeric: Singular stiffness matrix at x = {x} ({dof}). The system is kinematically unstable.

report.title: Calculation steps
report.unavailable: The calculation steps are available after a successful analysis.

loadSetKind.case: A single load case is investigated (factor 1.0).
loadSetKind.combo: The selected combination is investigated (all spans loaded).
loadSetKind.envelope: For the envelope the calculation steps of its first combination are shown.

report.patternNote: With pattern loading the envelopes follow from superposition of the span-wise solutions; the calculation steps show full loading.
report.s4: 4  Global stiffness matrix and load vector
report.s5: 5  Boundary conditions and system of equations
report.s7: 7  Internal forces and deflections per interval
report.siNote: All values of the calculation steps in SI units: N, m, Pa, rad. Signs: x to the right, z downwards, θ = dw/dx positive clockwise.
report.meshNote: Automatic meshing: {n} nodes at all characteristic points, {e} elements, {d} degrees of freedom (u, w, θ per node).
report.dofTable: Numbering of the degrees of freedom
report.hingeMethod: Hinges are modelled as double nodes: both sides share the DOFs u and w but have separate rotations θ_L and θ_R, so no moment is transferred (M = 0). A point moment at a hinge is assigned to the selected side.
report.keIntro: Plane frame element with the DOFs [u₁, w₁, θ₁, u₂, w₂, θ₂]; axial (EA) and bending (EI) stiffness:
report.portrait: Sparsity pattern of the global stiffness matrix
report.portraitBand: The global stiffness matrix is banded (half bandwidth b = {b}).
report.bandwise: row-wise, only columns within the band
report.equivIntro: Equivalent nodal forces of a linearly varying distributed load on an element of length L:
report.timoEquiv: Timoshenko: the exact fixed-end forces including shear deformation are used (identical for uniform load).
report.springsAdded: Springs added to the main diagonal
report.solverNote: Partitioning into {nf} free and {ns} restrained DOFs (no penalty method). Solution by Cholesky factorisation K_ff = L·Lᵀ (bandwidth {b}) with iterative refinement. Smallest relative pivot d/K_ii = {piv}.
report.displacements: Displacement vector [u, w, θ] per node
report.equilibriumIntro: Global equilibrium of the original loads (not the equivalent nodal loads) with the support and spring forces (moment about x = 0, clockwise positive):
report.endForces: The element end forces follow from the nodal displacements; inside the element the internal forces are obtained exactly from equilibrium with the distributed load.
report.endCheck: Check at ξ = L: M = {M} N·m, V = {V} N, w = {w} m

hand.intro: Statically determinate system: {r} support reactions, 3 equilibrium conditions and {h} hinge condition(s) M = 0.
hand.springs: Hand calculation not available: the system contains spring supports.
hand.indeterminate: The system is {n}-fold statically indeterminate – no classical hand calculation, the FEM solution applies.
hand.singular: The equilibrium conditions have no unique solution.
hand.signs: Reactions in the global system: forces positive in +x and +z (downwards), moments clockwise.
hand.sections: Method of sections: M(x) from the left part at the characteristic points, left (⁻) and right (⁺) of the position.
hand.sectionTable: Bending moments: hand calculation and FEM

report.periValues: Section values of the PERI component {name} (source: {src}):
report.periPerm: Check with permissible internal forces (perm F = R_d / γ_F, γ_F = 1.5) under the actual loads.
report.periDesign: Cross-section check per PERI (ST_was_2024/00040) with the interaction n–v, v–m, n–v–m, ρ = (2·max(0.5; v) − 1)², for the sections A 4-4, A 5-5 and B 2-2.
report.upliftNote: Pinned and roller supports transfer compression only; R_z > 0 (uplift, global z axis downwards) means the support fails.
report.periGirder: Check with the design values of the MULTIFLEX instructions for assembly and use: V_Ed ≤ V_Rd, M_Ed ≤ M_Rd, support force F_Ed ≤ F_R,d per support case (end/intermediate support, position to the nodes or distance from the girder end), for GT 24 the moment at the support M_Ed ≤ M_m,Rd; minimum distance of the end supports from the girder end.
report.periEc3: Cross-section check per EN 1993-1-1 6.2.10 with 6.2.9.1 (6.36), procedure after Wagenknecht, net section with bolt holes (PERI proof ST_kls_2016-00106).
report.periLattice: Member model as the PERI RSTAB model (continuous chords, pin-ended diagonals, gap nodes, standard between elastic couplers). Checks after PERI: ULS – cross-sections of chords (n, v, m) and diagonals (n, v, m_N), without buckling and welds; standard – flexural buckling (curve b, L_cr); couplers – slipping (15 / 25 kN : 1.1); ULS Flex – permissible loads of the PERI configurations. ULA HD: EN 1999-1-1 with heat affected zone.
report.latticeTable: Member list: axial force of the governing load arrangement, utilisation η as envelope of all ULS load arrangements.
report.flexTable: permissible loads of the PERI configuration (PI 550) ×1.5; uniform load and single loads added (on the safe side), a single load between connectors with the smaller resistance; self weight and decks included in the resistances.

import.title: Import beam list

rule.supports: Supports: all pinned (fixed). Beams with a single stand rest on the structure with the other end – a pinned support is added at that beam end.
rule.loads: Loads: vertical point loads, Gk as permanent load G, Qk as imposed load Q (characteristic); combinations: ULS 1.5·G + 1.5·Q and 1.0·G + 1.5·Q, SLS 1.0·G + 1.0·Q.
rule.length: Length: catalogue length of the designation (e.g. RCS 248 → 2480 mm); deviations up to 25 mm are adjusted, larger ones reported.
rule.selfWeight: Self weight of the PERI profile is included.

note.oneSupport: beams with a single support – mechanism, add supports
note.ground: continuously bedded on the ground – simplified with supports at the ends and under every load
note.profileMapped: profile not in the catalogue – nearest PERI profile used
note.lengthSnapped: length adjusted to the catalogue length (≤ 25 mm)
note.lengthFromDesignation: length in the file does not match the designation – catalogue length used
note.lengthNotCatalog: no catalogue length – length from the file used
note.outside: load/support outside the beam – moved to the beam end
note.endSupport: beams with one stand – pinned support added at the other beam end (resting on the structure)
note.endSupports: beams without supports in the drawing – pinned supports added at both ends

warn.noSupports: No supports in the file. Please add supports.
warn.ground: Continuously bedded on the ground – simplified: supports at the ends and under every load.
warn.profileMapped: Profile “{name}” not in the catalogue – using {profile}.
warn.lengthSnapped: Length {from} mm adjusted to the catalogue length {to} mm.
warn.lengthFromDesignation: Length in the file {from} mm does not match {name} – catalogue length {to} mm used.
warn.lengthNotCatalog: Length {L} mm is not a catalogue length (nearest: {near} mm) – calculated with the length from the file.
warn.outside: {name} at x = {x} mm lies outside the beam – moved to the beam end.
warn.endSupport: Only one stand in the drawing – second (pinned) support added at the beam end x = {x} mm (resting on the structure). Please check.
warn.endSupports: No supports in the drawing – pinned supports added at both beam ends. Please check.
warn.flexSpacing: Connector spacing {a} m matches no ULS Flex element (1.00 / 1.25 / 1.50 m) – rounded.

lattice.title: Member model
lattice.hint: Hover a member: section, internal forces, utilisation.
lattice.legendN: Blue = tension, red = compression (as in RSTAB); envelope: max solid, min dashed. Reactions R_z in global axes (↓ +).
lattice.legendM: Bending moments of chords and posts (web members pin-ended: M = 0). Reactions R_z in global axes (↓ +).

scaffold.title: Scaffold from PERI CAD
scaffold.intro: Open a PERI CAD drawing – two files: the DXF and the PERIEXPORT file (…⁠_peri.txt). The program recognises the PERI UP parts, builds the system in 3D, finds the lattice girders ULA / ULS / ULS Flex with their supports and loads and analyses the scaffold as a space frame.
scaffold.closeConfirm: Close the drawing? It can be opened again from the DXF.
scaffold.back: Back to the scaffold (3D, all girders)
scaffold.next: Preliminary design: utilisations above 70 % are checked by the structural engineer.

drop.title: Open both files of the drawing: .dxf and …⁠_peri.txt
drop.hint: Drop both files here or choose them together (Ctrl + click): the drawing .dxf and the export …⁠_peri.txt.
drop.stepsTitle: How to prepare the files in AutoCAD
drop.step1: Open the drawing in AutoCAD with PERI CAD loaded.
drop.step2: Load the script PERIEXPORT.lsp (command APPLOAD) and run the command PERIEXPORT. The file “<drawing name>⁠_peri.txt” with the parts of the older PERI CAD kind (spindles, diagonals, girders etc.) appears next to the drawing. The drawing is not changed.
drop.dwgNote: DWG is not read directly. Without the file …⁠_peri.txt the parts of the older PERI CAD kind are missing from the model: AutoCAD does not write them to the DXF.
drop.what1: 3D model of the scaffold from all parts of the drawing (DXF + export), parts list with weights.
drop.what2: Parts placed inaccurately are moved to their connection points; the remarks on the drawing show what to correct.
drop.what3: Space-frame analysis of the whole scaffold by the approval Z-8.22-863: standards, ledgers, rosette nodes, diagonals, wind at the site, second order – with the answer whether the scaffold works and recommendations.
drop.what4: Lattice girders ULA / ULS / ULS Flex with the PERI checks in the beam calculator; printable report.
drop.hintAdd: Drop another drawing here (.dxf with …⁠_peri.txt) or only the …⁠_peri.txt for the open drawing.
drop.step4: Open both files here together: .dxf and …⁠_peri.txt.

advice.title: Does the scaffold work?

verdict.check: The scaffold works, with little reserve

verdictText.none: Check the remarks below and choose “Calculate”. The default settings fit every PERI UP Flex scaffold.
verdictText.model: The result is not reliable yet: the model has errors to be put right before judging.
verdictText.fail: Largest utilisation {eta} %. What to change is listed below.
verdictText.check: Largest utilisation {eta} % (70 to 100 %): hand it to the structural engineer or strengthen after the recommendations below.
verdictText.ok: Largest utilisation {eta} % – enough reserve for a preliminary design.

advice.remarks: Remarks on the model: {n} – check them, they may affect the result.
advice.fixTitle: To put right in the model
advice.todoTitle: Where the reserve is small and what can be strengthened
advice.todoTitleFail: What to change so that the scaffold works
advice.details: Details of the analysis (combinations, checks, bases, assumptions)

fix.duplicates: Parts drawn twice at the same place: {n} places ({names}). Delete the extra ones in the drawing – their weight counts twice.
fix.defect: Error of the program building the model ({n} parts) – do not use the results, please report.
fix.mechanism: The structure is a mechanism in the combinations {names}: diagonals, supports or fixings to the building are missing.
fix.unheld: Parts not held by anything: {n} – check their connections in the drawing.
fix.notConverged: The analysis did not converge in the combinations {names} – results there are approximate.
fix.loose: Load-bearing parts not in the frame: {name} – {n} pcs. Check in the drawing what they connect to.
fix.lost: Parts not in the model: {name} – {n} pcs.
fix.noMaxWind: No site given: the maximum wind is not applied (working wind 0.2 kN/m² only). Give the site in the card “Site and conditions”.
fix.slender: The scaffold is tall and narrow (height = {r} × width) and not fixed to the building. If it is held on site, enter that in the card “Fixings to the building”; otherwise ballast will be needed.
fix.noWindZone: No wind zone (area) is found for the chosen site – the maximum wind is missing (working wind 0.2 kN/m² only). Choose the zone in the card “Site and conditions”.
fix.noVb0: There is no built-in wind map for the chosen site – the maximum wind is missing (working wind 0.2 kN/m² only). Enter v_b,0 from the national annex or q_p directly in the card “Site and conditions”.
fix.noQp: q_p of the maximum wind is entered by hand as 0 – the maximum wind is missing. Enter q_p in the card “Site and conditions”.

do.rootHorizontal: Main cause: the scaffold carries the horizontal load along {axis} poorly. Start with fixings to the building or diagonals in that direction – the other overloads below will get smaller.
do.stabilityLost: Stability lost in the combinations {names}{dir}: the frame does not carry the horizontal load. Add diagonals in that direction over the whole height, fix the scaffold to the building or reduce the lift height.
do.uplift: Bases have to hold the scaffold down ({n} pcs){dir}: add ballast on the bottom ledgers, widen the base or fix the scaffold to the building.
do.node: Ledger – standard nodes: {n} parts, up to {eta} %{dir}. Add diagonals in these bays (they relieve the nodes), reduce the standard spacing or the load.
do.standard: Standards and their joints: {n} parts, up to {eta} %{dir}. Add standards under the load, diagonals or ledgers against bending, or reduce the load.
do.ledger: Ledgers: {n} parts, up to {eta} %. Reduce the span (intermediate standard), use a reinforced ledger UHV or a lattice girder, reduce the deck load.
do.diagonal: Diagonals: {n} parts, up to {eta} %{dir}. Add diagonals in neighbouring bays and lifts of the same plane or fix the scaffold to the building.
do.jack: Base jacks: {n} parts, up to {eta} %. Reduce the jack extension or spread the load over more standards.
do.tie: Anchors and fixings to the building: {n} parts, up to {eta} %{dir}. Add fixing points or diagonals to relieve them.
do.lifted: Bases lifting off: {n} (allowed, but the scaffold rocks). Ballast or a fixing to the building reduce the displacements.
do.sway: Horizontal displacement {mm} mm (height / {ratio}): the frame is soft. Add diagonals or fixings to the building.
do.girder: Lattice girder {name}: {eta} %. Open it in the beam calculator; reduce the span or the load or use a deeper girder.
do.coupler: Tubes on couplers: {n} parts, up to {eta} %{dir}. The coupler may slip on the tube: add a safety coupler right next to the loaded one or replace the tube by a PERI UP ledger or diagonal.
do.ledgerSway: Ledgers: {n} parts, up to {eta} %{dir} – bending from the sway of the scaffold under wind, not from the deck load. Add diagonals in the adjacent bays or a fixing to the building: they take the moment off the ledgers.
do.bracket: Brackets: {n} parts, up to {eta} %{dir}. Use a shorter bracket, a smaller field width or load on the bracket deck, or put a standard under the bracket.

loads.title: User loads

calc.title: Scaffold analysis (space frame)
calc.intro: The scaffold is analysed as a space frame, as in PERI ForceControl: continuous standards, ledgers with semi-rigid rosette connections, diagonals (without slack), lattice girders connected at both chords, anchors, bases without tension. Loads and combinations after DIN EN 12811-1 (γF = 1.5), stiffness and node checks after the approval Z-8.22-863.
calc.combosIndoor: Indoors: G + Q on one level + notional horizontal load 2.5 % of Q, in 4 directions.
calc.combosNoMax: Outdoors: G + Q + working wind 0.2 kN/m², in 4 directions. No maximum wind set (card “Site and conditions”) – no out-of-service condition.
calc.combosOutdoor: Outdoors: working (G + Q + wind 0.2 kN/m²) and out of service (G + share of Q + maximum wind {q}), 4 directions each.

calc.unstable: Combinations {names}: the system is a mechanism or unstable – bracing or supports are missing.
calc.comboLegend: A – working, R – out of service (maximum wind, γ = 1.5), S – stability (permanent γ = 0.9, maximum wind); ±x, ±y – direction of wind and sway. Displacements and ΣV – design values.
calc.basesMax: Largest vertical force {v}, horizontal force {h} (design values).
calc.uplift: Uplift (tension) at {n} bases – ballast or anchoring needed. Show.

export.errNoDxf: Open the DXF of the drawing first, then the file …⁠_peri.txt.

level.what: Deck level that carries the service load of the load class.
level.why: By EN 12811-1 the full service load acts on one level; the other levels carry their self weight (and snow).
level.effect: “Automatic” takes the level with the largest deck area – the largest total load. Another level distributes the forces in standards and ledgers differently: choose it if that level will be loaded.

g.what: Self weight of the decks per m² of deck area.
g.why: The weight of the members of the drawing is computed from the catalogue; the decks are taken as an area load.
g.effect: Permanent load in all combinations (γ = 1.5; in the S combinations γ = 0.9) and in the beam loads for the beam calculator. Default 0.3 kN/m² – with a reserve for PERI UP decks.

tol.what: Largest distance over which a part of the drawing is moved onto its connection point.
tol.why: In drawings parts often sit millimetres to centimetres off the rosettes and axes; without snapping they would not connect and the model would fall apart.
tol.effect: Larger – more parts are connected, but a value too large also connects parts that are not connected in reality. 0 – off. Default 5 cm, at most 20 cm.

ubk.what: Model of the UBK diagonals: by Annex A of the approval (eccentric head, tab. A.1/A.2) or simplified centric (tab. 15).
ubk.why: The diagonals give the scaffold its horizontal stiffness; the forces in diagonals and nodes and the displacements depend on their model.
ubk.effect: “Annex A” matches the approval Z-8.22-863 and PERI ForceControl – default. “Tab. 15” is a simplified variant for comparison: other stiffness and distribution of forces.

slack.what: Play in the connection of the diagonals that is taken up before the diagonal carries.
slack.why: The approval allows the play of the wedge connections to be considered; PERI ForceControl calculates without it.
slack.effect: “Per approval” – the diagonals carry only after the play: larger displacements, part of the forces goes into the nodes of the standards. Default – no slack, as PFC.

splice.what: Whether the joints of the standards (spigots) carry tension.
splice.why: A joint that is not secured carries compression only: under tension it opens.
splice.effect: “No tension” – the joint opens under tension, as in PFC; safer for the check of uplift and overturning (default). “With tension” – only if the joints are secured with bolts or spring pins.

cap.what: Where the resistance of the nodes (rosettes) and diagonals is taken from.
cap.why: The approval gives different values for standards with 6 and 8 mm rosettes; the stiffness of the model is always that for 6 mm.
cap.effect: “By the article” – for each standard by its article, as PFC (default). “As the stiffness: 6 mm” – the smaller values for all standards, with a reserve.

second.what: Second-order analysis with an inclination of the standards of 1/200 and bow imperfections of the standards.
second.why: A scaffold is a flexible structure; EN 12811-1 requires deformations and imperfections to be considered.
second.effect: Switch off for comparison only: forces and displacements come out smaller than in reality, a loss of stability is not found. Default – on.

gFavR.what: Additional S combinations: permanent loads with γ = 0.9, without service load, with the maximum wind.
gFavR.why: They check bases lifting off and light scaffolds overturning – as the “Stability” section of PERI ForceControl.
gFavR.effect: On – lifting off and overturning are found that the combinations with γ = 1.5 do not show. Off can hide missing ballast or ties. Acts only outdoors with a maximum wind. Default – on.

exposure.what: Where the scaffold stands: outdoors or indoors.
exposure.why: Wind, snow and ice depend on it.
exposure.effect: “Outdoors” – working wind 0.2 kN/m² and the maximum wind of the site (combinations R and S). “Indoors” – no wind, snow or ice; instead of wind a notional horizontal load of 2.5 % of the service load (at least 0.3 kN) acts.

terrain.what: Terrain category by EN 1991-1-4: 0 – sea, I – lakes, II – open country, III – suburbs, IV – town.
terrain.why: The roughness of the terrain changes how the wind speed grows with height.
terrain.effect: The lower the category, the larger q_p. Acts for the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg and other countries; in Germany q_p follows from the wind zone and the location, the category has no effect. Default II.

windManual.what: Enter the peak velocity pressure q_p of the maximum wind directly.
windManual.why: When the wind is given by the project or the client, or the site cannot be determined.
windManual.effect: The q_p entered is used as it is for the combinations R and S: site, zone and the factor 0.7 are not applied.

qMax.what: Peak velocity pressure of the maximum wind at the height of the scaffold.
qMax.why: Sets the wind out of service.
qMax.effect: The wind load of the combinations R and S is proportional to q_p; 0 – no out-of-service combinations.

windZone.what: Wind zone 1–4 in Germany by DIN EN 1991-1-4/NA.
windZone.why: The zone sets the basic wind velocity.
windZone.effect: “Automatic” – zone from the DIBt table for the district of the site; if the district lies in several zones, choose the zone yourself. The higher the zone, the larger q_p.

windExposure.what: Location by the NA: inland, coast or islands of the North Sea and the Baltic.
windExposure.why: For the coast and the islands the NA gives own q_p profiles.
windExposure.effect: Coast and islands give a larger q_p than inland.

windAreaNL.what: Wind area I–III of the Netherlands by NEN-EN 1991-1-4/NB.
windAreaNL.why: The area sets the basic wind velocity v_b,0 = 29.5 / 27 / 24.5 m/s.
windAreaNL.effect: “Automatic” – by the municipality of the site. Area I gives the largest q_p.

vb0Select.what: Basic wind velocity v_b,0 by the national annex (Belgium – by municipality, Luxembourg – 24 m/s).
vb0Select.why: Sets q_p together with the terrain category and the height of the scaffold.
vb0Select.effect: “Automatic” – by the site. q_p grows with the square of v_b,0.

vb0.what: Basic wind velocity v_b,0 from the national annex to EN 1991-1-4 of the country where the scaffold stands.
vb0.why: For countries without a built-in wind map the program does not know v_b,0.
vb0.effect: q_p is computed by EN 1991-1-4 with the terrain category and the height of the scaffold and grows with the square of v_b,0. 0 – no maximum wind: no out-of-service combinations.

standing.what: Reduction of the maximum wind by the factor 0.7 for the limited time the scaffold stands (EN 12811-1).
standing.why: Scaffolds stand for a short time, so a wind with a shorter return period than for buildings may be used.
standing.effect: q_p of the maximum wind is multiplied by 0.7. Switch off if the project or the national code requires the full wind. Default – on.

snow.why: In winter snow on the decks is an additional vertical load out of service.
snow.effect: In the R combinations snow on all decks is added (γ = 1.5); its value is entered in the analysis card.

snowLoad.what: Snow load per m² of deck.
snowLoad.why: Depends on the site and on whether the decks are cleared.
snowLoad.effect: Acts on all levels in the R combinations with γ = 1.5. Default 0.75 kN/m².

ice.why: Ice adds weight and increases the area the wind acts on.
ice.effect: A layer of ice is added to all members: more self weight and wind load in all combinations; the thickness is entered in the analysis card.

iceThickness.what: Thickness of the ice layer on the members.
iceThickness.why: Sets the additional weight (900 kg/m³) and the width of the members for the wind.
iceThickness.effect: The width of each member for the wind grows by two thicknesses, the weight by that of the ice shell. Default 1 cm.

loadClass.what: Load class by EN 12811-1 (1–6): uniform service load on the deck from 0.75 to 6.0 kN/m².
loadClass.why: Sets what may be put on the scaffold: people, material, equipment.
loadClass.effect: The service load acts on the loaded level in the working combinations A; out of service (R) with the share 0 % (class 1), 25 % (2–3) or 50 % (4–6). Higher class – larger forces.

loadName.what: Name of the load for the table and the report.
loadName.why: So that the load can be recognised in the list and in the report.

loadCase.what: Kind of load: permanent (G) or variable (Q).
loadCase.why: Permanent loads always act, variable loads while the scaffold is used.
loadCase.effect: G – in all combinations with γ = 1.5 (in S γ = 0.9). Q – fully in the working combinations, out of service with the share by the load class.

loadKind.what: Type of load: a point force at one point of the part or a uniform load along it.
loadKind.why: Supports, equipment and reactions of structures set on top are mostly forces, distributed loads line loads.
loadKind.effect: Point – a force on each selected part at “Position, %”; line – a load per length over the whole length of each selected part.

loadDir.what: Direction of the load: vertically down (Z) or horizontal along the X or Y axis of the drawing.
loadDir.why: Horizontal forces – for example from a hoist, a bracing cable or a structure set on top.
loadDir.effect: A horizontal load acts in each combination in its direction: in +x and −x with the respective sign (as the hoist loads LC7/LC8 in PFC).

loadWhen.what: In which combinations the load acts.
loadWhen.why: Some loads exist only while working (material on the platform), others only out of service (stored material, structure in the parking position).
loadWhen.effect: “Working and out of service” – Q out of service with the share by the load class; “working only” – only in the A combinations; “out of service only” – fully in the R combinations.

loadValue.what: Size of the load: a force for a point or a load per length for a line, characteristic (without partial factors).
loadValue.why: The program applies the partial factors itself.
loadValue.effect: Acts fully on each selected part and is not shared between them.

loadAt.what: Position of the point force along the part, % of the length from its start.
loadAt.why: The force may act away from a node.
loadAt.effect: 0 and 100 % – ends of the part, 50 % – middle. Start – the end with the smaller X (then Y), for standards the lower one.

plan.what: Loads drawn in the drawing as blocks with a weight (ballast, containers): the weight goes onto the parts under their outline.
plan.why: So that these loads need not be entered by hand.
plan.effect: On – the weight of the blocks as a permanent load on the parts below. Switch off if these loads are entered by hand, otherwise they are counted twice. Default – on.

dhb.what: Dynamic horizontal load DHB when a load is set down on the platform by a crane (as in PERI ForceControl).
dhb.why: A load set down by a crane pushes the platform sideways.
dhb.effect: In the working combinations share × load (γ = 1.5) is added on the selected parts or the heads of the standards; indoors DHB replaces the notional horizontal load of the decks. Acts only if a load is entered.

dhbLoad.what: Weight of the load the crane sets down on the platform (characteristic).

dhbShare.what: Share of the weight of the load that acts horizontally.
dhbShare.effect: The horizontal force grows with the share. Default 10 %.

dhbDir.what: In which directions of the working combinations DHB acts.
dhbDir.why: If the direction the load is set down from is known, it can be limited.
dhbDir.effect: ±x, ±y – in all four working combinations (default); ±x or ±y – only in the combinations of that direction.

fixName.what: Name of the fixing for the table and the report.
fixName.why: So that the fixing can be recognised in the list and in the report.

fixAxes.what: Axes X, Y, Z of the drawing in which the fixing holds the part.
fixAxes.why: A wall tie usually holds horizontally, a support on a structure vertically.
fixAxes.effect: In the axes chosen the node is held both ways (compression and tension), in the others it is free. The reactions are shown in the table of fixings and in the report.

fixAt.what: Position of the fixing along the part, % of the length from its start.
fixAt.why: The fixing may sit away from the ends of the part.
fixAt.effect: 0 and 100 % – ends, 50 % – middle. Start – the end with the smaller X (then Y), for standards the lower one.

fixLimit.what: Design resistance of one fixing (for example of a tie).
fixLimit.why: So that the program checks the fixing.
fixLimit.effect: If entered – the resultant reaction is compared with it (check “fixing”, η). 0 – no check, reactions only.

deck.what: Whether a deck lies on the ledger or bracket.
deck.why: The deck passes its weight and the working load to the ledger or bracket.
deck.effect: On – load from the field width on the part: self weight of the deck and, if ticked, the working load of the load class. Off – no load from a deck.

width.what: Field width of the deck across the section – length of the decks between this section and the neighbouring ones.
width.why: In a row of equal fields the section carries half a field on each side, one field in all.
width.effect: Load on the ledger or bracket = load per m² × field width, kN/m along the part. Wider field – larger load.

work.what: The working load of the load class acts on this deck.
work.why: By EN 12811-1 the working load stands on the deck where people work; the others carry their self weight.
work.effect: On – q of the class × field width (fully in service, out of service with the share of the class). Indoors the notional horizontal load of 2.5 % is added.

ext.what: Distance from the base plate of the jack to the bottom of the standard on it.
ext.why: The jack levels the height; the larger the extension, the weaker the jack.
ext.effect: Changes the height of the standards on the jack and the check of the jack (N + M). Largest value by the article.

field.what: Field width a new deck on a ledger or bracket gets.
field.why: Usually all fields of a scaffold are equal – so it need not be entered each time.
field.effect: Only for new decks; for existing ones the width is changed in the properties of the part.

qMax.what: Peak velocity pressure of the maximum wind for scaffolds outdoors.
qMax.why: Sets the out-of-service combinations R and S (maximum wind, uplift and overturning).
qMax.effect: The wind of R and S acts on a band of 0.2 m at each deck over the field width and on the parts of the section. 0 – working wind 0.2 kN/m² only. Nets and sheeting are not considered.

about.what: The section built from PERI UP parts is calculated with the same analysis as scaffolds from PERI CAD: space frame with semi-rigid rosette nodes, second order, checks by the approval Z-8.22-863.
about.why: So that a section can be checked without a PERI CAD drawing.
about.effect: The section is a plane frame; out of its plane it is held by the longitudinal bracing. Loads: deck and working load from the field width, wind on the parts of the section, anchors hold in X, supports are the base plates of the jacks.

families.what: Series of PERI UP parts shown in the catalogue of the designer.
families.why: Parts of one generation are used: the first (UVR, UVH, UH Plus, UBK) or the second (UVR-2, UVH-2, UH-2, UBK-2 with the 8 mm rosette).
families.effect: Hidden series do not appear in the catalogue; parts already placed stay and are calculated by their article. Default – first generation.

anchorDir.what: On which side of the standard the wall (building) is that the anchor is fixed to.
anchorDir.why: In the drawing the anchor goes to the wall; it shows which standards stand at the facade and where they are tied.
anchorDir.effect: The anchor holds the standard horizontally (X) both ways – tension and compression; the side of the wall decides how it is drawn and where its force points in the report.

viewPoints.what: Which checks of the nodes (standard + ledgers at the rosette) and of the joints of the standards are shown on the drawing as circles with percent.
viewPoints.why: There are many nodes – the threshold leaves only the loaded ones.
viewPoints.effect: “All” – every node and joint; “from a utilisation” – only from the value entered; “none” – no circles. No effect on the analysis.

viewReactions.what: Reactions of the supports (under the base plates of the jacks) and forces of the anchors on the drawing after the analysis.
viewReactions.why: To see the load on the ground and on the fixings to the building.
viewReactions.effect: V – largest vertical reaction (and V_min when lifting off), H – largest horizontal, over all combinations; at an anchor its largest force. No effect on the analysis.

viewShear.what: Shear force diagram V of the ledgers, brackets and standards: from the combination with the largest value.
viewShear.why: To see which force goes from the ledger into the node and how the standards carry the horizontal load.
viewShear.effect: Values at the ends of the member in kN (design values, with γ = 1.5). No effect on the analysis.

deckClass.what: Load class EN 12811-1 of this deck: working load from 0.75 to 6.0 kN/m².
deckClass.why: The load may differ between levels and brackets; the class is kept with each ledger or bracket.
deckClass.effect: Working load of this deck = load of the class × field width; it acts if “Working load” is ticked. On the drawing the class is written at the arrows.

classNew.what: Load class a new deck gets.
classNew.why: Usually a scaffold has one class – so it need not be entered each time.
classNew.effect: Only for new decks: a placed deck keeps its own class, changed in the properties of the part.

designer.title: Scaffold section (side view)
designer.intro: Choose a part in the catalogue and move over the drawing: it snaps to the nearest connection point (green – can be placed). Standards on jacks, base standards and each other, ledgers and diagonals between rosettes of equal height, brackets on a rosette. A standard can hang on a diagonal and a ledger – a bracket built from a diagonal. Wheel – zoom, right button – pan, band – select several, Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V – copy a group, Del – delete, Ctrl+Z – undo. A second equal diagonal in the same bay goes on the other side of the rosette (double, dashed). An anchor is selected by a click or a band and deleted with Del.
designer.exampleConfirm: Replace the current section by the example (facade scaffold 0.75 m)?
designer.clearConfirm: Delete all parts of the section?
designer.etaLegend: Colour of the parts by utilisation η:

props.title: Properties
props.none: Select a part in the drawing (Ctrl/Shift + click – several).
props.anchors: Anchors on this standard (height of the rosette, m):

designer.name: Name of the section
designer.assumptions: The section is calculated as a plane frame: out of its plane the scaffold is held by the longitudinal bracing. Loads on ledgers and brackets from the field width. The wind acts on a band at each deck over the field width (0.4 m at the working level, 0.2 m at the others) and on the parts of the section; indoors and with little wind the notional horizontal load of 2.5 % of the working load (at least 0.3 kN).

hint.part: Click – place the part where shown. Esc – leave the tool.
hint.noSnap: This part cannot go here: move it to a rosette or a support point.
hint.tube1: Tube: click the first point on a standard.
hint.tube2: Tube: click the second point on another standard (couplers are added).
hint.anchor: Anchor: click a point on a standard, then show on which side the wall is.
hint.select: Click – select a part, band with the left button – several, right button – pan the drawing. Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V – copy and paste.
hint.paste: Paste: the group follows the pointer (0.25 m, in height 0.5 m – rosettes on the grid). Click – place, several times; Esc – leave.
hint.anchor2: Anchor: move the pointer to the wall – left of the standard (wall on the left) or right (wall on the right); click – place, Esc – cancel.

issue.floating: Standards stand on nothing – put a jack or another standard under them.
issue.noDecks: No deck: tick “Deck on the part” at ledgers or brackets.
issue.noWork: No working load anywhere: tick it at a deck.
issue.noBracing: Neither diagonals nor anchors: the section is not braced horizontally.

designer.familiesHint: Which series of parts the catalogue shows.
designer.pointsLegend: Circles – checks of the nodes (standard + ledgers at the rosette) and the joints of the standards, at their place.

view.title: Display of the result
view.points: Nodes and joints on the drawing
view.reactions: Reactions of the supports and forces of the anchors

designer.unstable: The section loses its stability (sway): add diagonals or anchors
